Done. View transitions are wired up following the patterns in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/view-transitions.md` — this Next version needs no config flag, and `<ViewTransition>` comes straight from `react`.

**What changed**

`app/ProductGrid.tsx` — each thumbnail is wrapped in `<ViewTransition name={`product-${slug}`} share="morph" default="none">`, and its `<Link>` carries `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}`.

`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx` — the hero uses the *same* `name`, forming the morph pair. The hero deliberately stays outside the Suspense boundary so it renders in the same commit as the navigation (a fallback in between would break the pair). The back link is tagged `transitionTypes={['nav-back']}`.

`app/page.tsx` / detail page — both wrap their root element in a directional `<ViewTransition>`, and both wrap the Suspense fallback in `exit="slide-down"` with the content in `enter="slide-up"`. The directional wrappers are in the pages rather than the layout, since layouts persist across navigation and never fire enter/exit.

`app/transitions.ts` — the shared type→class map (`nav-forward`/`nav-back`, `default: 'none'`) so typeless transitions (browser back, `router.refresh()`, Suspense reveals) don't slide sideways.

`app/globals.css` — the morph (400ms with a mid-flight blur to hide interpolation as the aspect ratio goes 4/3 → 1/1), asymmetric skeleton→content timing (150ms exit, enter fading in after it), 60px directional slides, `::view-transition { pointer-events: none }` so clicks aren't swallowed mid-animation, and a `prefers-reduced-motion` block zeroing all durations and delays (plus the looping skeleton pulse).

`react-canary.d.ts` — `ViewTransition` is declared in `@types/react/canary.d.ts`, which `next-env.d.ts` doesn't reference, so this one-line reference makes it visible to TypeScript.

**Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` and `next build` both clean; served HTML shows matching `vt-name="product-classic-sneakers"` with `vt-share="morph"` on both the thumbnail and the hero; all `::view-transition-*(.class)` rules and the reduced-motion `!important` overrides survive minification. I traced the directional path through the framework too — `Link` → `addTransitionType` → React's `getClassNameByType`, which resolves the per-type object client-side (which is why SSR emits only `vt-update="none"` on the page roots; there's no navigation type during a server render).

Two notes: the guide's header-anchoring step doesn't apply here, as this app has no persistent header to anchor. And on the home page the Suspense boundary wraps a synchronous `ProductGrid`, so its fallback never actually renders — I wired the reveal anyway to match the detail page, where the 100ms delay does show the skeleton.
